rv.q: In general, my view of Blank's plucky work in town so far is that its artistic leadership has to find ways to produce these musicals in ways that depart more radically from traditional stagings and that match both their spaces and the young talent they're able to recruit.
All in all, Blank has given Chicago good reason to discover (or rediscover) this hidden Sondheim gem.
I am happy to report that Blank Theatre has once again knocked it clean out of the park.
And Blank Theatre’s production is a little gem, proof-positive of the piece earning its keep in the Sondheim canon.
To put it simply, Passion is a feat.
Between the haunting set created by Hayley E Wallenfeldt and the cast of gorgeous voices, Sondheim and Lapine’s strange baby deserves its flowers.

Like Curley's wife in Of Mice and Men , Brown's Fosca is as much a lonely victim as a schemer, and someone who has been defined (and gossiped about) by the men around her most of her life (including the callow count who married her for money as a teen and left her destitute).
For any Sondheim fan, this production is a must; for anyone who has not seen Passion before, it can be a challenging and ultimately rewarding revelation.

cn.t: Critics praise this rarely-produced Sondheim work for its lush, challenging score and complex characters, calling it a dark masterpiece that showcases the composer's operatic ambitions and rewards adventurous audiences.
